feature: Explore every resident in a displayed cohort through inherited-trait bands
changes: An optional Explore variation in this cohort panel shows the current island, generation, species, resident count and lowest, mean and highest trait indices.
Five native trait-band buttons cover a fixed 0–100 domain. Each displays a count and a bar proportional to its share of the full displayed cohort.
Selecting a band reveals all its actual residents, ordered by raw trait mean and then ID. Native resident buttons use the existing island and organism selection path.
Unrounded indices remain available in a details view to explain values that round onto a displayed band boundary. Empty bands and empty cohorts have explicit messages.
Band choices are keyed to the founding frame, displayed frame, island and species, so changed contexts immediately suppress stale contents. Selecting bands does not automatically select an organism.
Exploration preserves the existing pinned comparison and captured observation. Native controls, visible selection states and responsive layouts support keyboard and phone use.
scientificCorrectness: Raw trait means, rather than rounded labels, determine contiguous half-open bands [0,.2), [.2,.4), [.4,.6), [.6,.8), with the last band [.8,1] including the upper endpoint.

Every actual resident of the displayed island and species is counted once. Counts and bar shares use the complete current cohort, including six-founder and empty cohorts, rather than a selected or random sample.
Sorting presentation records does not reorder or mutate the model population. Means and endpoints use actual inherited trait values; empty-cohort mean and range are described as undefined.
The panel explains that trait spread does not establish an evolutionary cause, measure genome-wide genetic diversity, or rank breeding success.
Only presentation state and the existing organism selection change. The evolutionary model, recorded history, world RNG, existing pin and captured evidence remain unchanged.
